stories.title: Valor, Point72 back General Intuition at $6B valuation as AI startup pushes into robotics
stories.simple_summary: A startup called General Intuition is trying to raise billions of dollars to build AI that controls robots. Big investors are interested in giving them the money.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors and engineers — nothing you need to act on right now.

stories.title: Japan to tap AI to speed up materials development 10-fold
stories.simple_summary: Japan's government plans to use AI to help scientists discover new materials and chemicals much faster than they can today.
stories.why_it_matters: This could eventually lead to better products (like stronger phone screens or lighter cars), but it's still very early.

stories.title: OpenAI is building AI agents for everything. Will everyone use them?
stories.simple_summary: OpenAI (the company behind ChatGPT) is working on AI agents — computer helpers that can do tasks for you automatically — and wants regular people to use them, not just software engineers.
stories.why_it_matters: You may soon be able to use AI to do everyday tasks on your computer or phone, like scheduling appointments or organizing files, without needing to be tech-savvy.

stories.title: Laid off for a bot, China’s workers face an AI jobs squeeze
stories.simple_summary: In China, workers are losing their jobs to AI and automation, similar to factory workers being replaced by machines decades ago.
stories.why_it_matters: This shows that AI automation is real and spreading — something to be aware of if you have employees or workers depending on certain jobs.

stories.title: Hugging Face reportedly in talks to be acquired for $13B
stories.simple_summary: A popular AI tools company called Hugging Face is getting offers to be bought for $13 billion, but the founders might not want to sell.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors — nothing you need to act on.

stories.title: Google brings Antigravity under Gemini Enterprise to provide granular spend controls
stories.simple_summary: Google added a control tool to its Gemini business AI product so companies can track and limit how much they're spending on it.
stories.why_it_matters: If your business uses Google's AI services, you may have better tools to manage your costs.

stories.title: Some of Russia’s A.I. Drones Are Powered by Nvidia Microcomputers, Ukrainian Officials Say
stories.simple_summary: Russian military drones are using Nvidia computer chips (made in the U.S.) to power their AI, according to Ukrainian officials.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to government and defense officials — nothing you need to act on.

stories.title: Taiwan issues indictments over alleged illegal export of AI servers to China
stories.simple_summary: Taiwan's government is charging people with illegally selling advanced AI computer servers to China, breaking export rules.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to geopolitics and large tech companies — nothing you need to act on.

stories.title: 'Don't ask me to print your ChatGPT birthday card': Hitting back at AI 'slop'
stories.simple_summary: People are getting tired of poorly-made, lazy AI-generated content (like greeting cards written by ChatGPT) and pushing back against it.
stories.why_it_matters: If you own a business, customers increasingly value genuine, human-made work — don't rely too heavily on AI for things that need a personal touch.

stories.title: AI is coming for your glasses
stories.simple_summary: Companies are working on putting AI features into glasses or eyewear devices you wear.
stories.why_it_matters: You may eventually see AI-powered glasses that can recognize things you're looking at or answer questions, but these products are still being developed.

stories.title: Who’s behind the new ‘stealth model’ Ox Alpha?
stories.simple_summary: A mysterious new AI model called Ox Alpha has appeared, and people on the internet are guessing who created it and what it can do.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to AI enthusiasts and tech investors — nothing you need to act on.

stories.title: Billionaires Stanley Druckenmiller and Dan Loeb Both Sold Broadcom and Piled Into This Virtual Monopoly Artificial Intelligence (AI) Stock Instead
stories.simple_summary: Two billionaire investors recently sold their shares in computer chip company Broadcom and bought shares in another AI-related company instead.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to stock investors — nothing you need to act on.
